## 0. How to read this volume
Every normative statement carries a stable requirement id `VOLB-nnn`. Section 10 maps each of this volume's findings (F-006, F-007, F-010, F-019) to its requirements and sections. Where this volume amends an earlier contract (DATA-MODEL.md rev 1.0, ENDPOINTS.md rev 1.0), the amendment is called out inline and controls on conflict.
Two identities appear throughout and must never be conflated (F-010):
- **Thread identity** — a CHD-owned logical conversation: a room (`obj-*`, `task-*`, `space-*`) plus a reply tree over that room's ordered log. Durable in DuckBrain. - **Hermes session identity** — the session id of a Hermes agent conversation, minted and owned by Hermes. CHD stores only a *reference* to it (the bond).
---

## 1. Storage substrate: what DuckBrain actually provides (F-019)
This section is normative context for every contract below. All claims are read from the pinned revision's README and `docs/api/http-api.md` on 2026-11-08.
**VOLB-001 (D1 — pinned dependency).** CHD builds against DuckBrain at revision `972aeb0023973b2d62186a748eab5ccede2dd0f8`. The build MUST re-verify the behavioral contracts relied on below (multi-version same-key semantics, durability headers, attribute filters) against the release tag actually deployed before M3 sign-off (VOLB-001).
**VOLB-002 (D2 — memories, not tables).** The deployed surface is a memory store: hierarchical slash-prefixed keys, JSONL append-only segments, DuckDB query layer, per-namespace git repos. **Generic REST over declared tables (SUPA-3/SUPA-6) and role grants/token lifecycle (DB-SUPA-4) are implemented on branch but NOT released** ("release evidence pending" per the pinned README). CHD MUST NOT use declared tables, MUST NOT assume server-side auth grants beyond `X-API-Key` authentication, and MUST NOT assume server-side schema validation (VOLB-002).
**D3 — Keys are slash-prefixed.** A DuckBrain memory key is a path like `/projects/myapp/database`. The pre-review contract notation omitted the leading slash (the F-019 defect); every key in this specification is normalized to the canonical **`/chd/...`** form. Section 2 defines the layout (VOLB-003).
**VOLB-004 (D4 — same-key writes are append-only multi-version).** N writes to one key produce N independent versions with distinct UUID `id`s; nothing is overwritten; a key has no privileged "current" version. `GET /api/memories/key/:key` returns the most recent **non-tombstoned** version ordered `timestamp DESC, id ASC`; the list route (`GET /api/memories`) returns all versions. The `timestamp DESC, id ASC` order is deterministic per dataset but is **not write order within one millisecond** — the `id` tiebreak is a random UUIDv4. The process-local serializer `seq` is not durable and is not a cursor (VOLB-004, VOLB-005).
**D5 — No durable ordering service-side.** Because of D4, DuckBrain provides **no durable room ordering** from its default timestamp/UUID ordering. CHD must allocate and carry its own sequence numbers (Section 5.1).
**VOLB-006 (D6 — write durability is per-namespace and mode-dependent).** Modes: `buffered` (default; page-cache append; process-kill safe, **OS crash/power loss can lose acked writes with an unbounded window**), `fsync` (fdatasync + directory fsync barrier before the 2xx; **RPO = 0 on a single node**), `direct` (O_DIRECT block framing; RPO = 0). Every successful write response carries `X-Durability` (mode achieved), `X-Durability-Configured` (mode configured), and — only when they differ — `X-Durability-Degraded`.
**VOLB-007 (D6 — durability failures are loud; git history and S3 are never the acknowledgement).** Durability failures are loud HTTP 500s with codes (`DURABILITY_FSYNC_FAILED`, `DURABILITY_UNSUPPORTED`, …); a failed write is **never acknowledged**. Git commits are debounced (~30 s default) and S3 push rides the same window — **git history and S3 are never the write acknowledgement**.
**VOLB-008 (D7 — read surface).** `GET /api/memories` supports `prefix`, `domain`, `author`, `q` (needs embeddings; CHD MUST NOT depend on it), `contains`, `after`/`before`/ `between` (ISO-8601), `attr.<name>=<value>` (repeatable), `historical`, `limit` (default 50), `offset`. Unknown query parameters are refused 400 (no silent ignoring); `?key=` is not a parameter of this route. `GET /api/memories/key/:key` returns the latest non-tombstoned version by key. `GET /api/keys/flat` lists keys by `prefix` with `limit`/`offset`. `GET /api/memories/:id` fetches one version by id (VOLB-008).
**VOLB-009 (D8 — tombstones and PUT).** `DELETE /api/memories/:id` appends a tombstone for one version; `PUT /api/memories/:id` tombstones the old version and appends a new one. Tombstoned versions are excluded from both current and historical list views. CHD treats delete as a retention operation only, never as part of a state machine transition (VOLB-009).
**D9 — Single namespace, single writer.** All CHD records live in the `chd` namespace (one git repo server-side). The **harness service is the ONLY writer** of every `/chd/*` key family (Section 2, R-028, CT-13); agents read rooms and write only through the harness API (Section 5; this AMENDS CT-05's "writer: the sending session via its role token" — see VOLB-020). One harness instance is authoritative per `chd` namespace; multi-writer harness replicas are out of scope for this revision (VOLB-010).
**D10 — Durability configuration for CHD (decision).** The operator MUST configure the `chd` namespace override to `fsync`:
```json { "durability": { "defaultMode": "buffered", "overrides": { "chd": "fsync" } } } ```
Rationale: every CHD record is control state whose loss on OS crash would violate F-007's acceptance (crashes neither lose an accepted request nor double-execute work). `buffered`'s unbounded power-loss window is unacceptable for the record families that carry the acceptance sequence of Section 6. `direct` adds nothing for this workload and requires block framing. The harness verifies on every write ack that `X-Durability` == `fsync` (VOLB-011).
**VOLB-011 (D11 — data classes and store separation; R31-016, R31-028).** CHD distinguishes four logical data classes; they are not interchangeable and not all share a consistency requirement. `coordination_report` and `control_key` are separate routing classes even though both are controller-authoritative in the default deployment:
| Class | Contents | Namespace | Consistency required | |---|---|---|---| | `coordination_report` | rooms, messages, reports, objective/assignment/criterion records, waits, audit | `chd` | **immediate** on the controller; `fsync` ack | | `control_key` | manifests, tickets, grants, bonds, registry and other protected `/chd/*` keys | `chd` | **immediate** on the controller; `fsync` ack | | `session_archive` | native Hermes session exports, archive manifests, checkpoint/gap records | `chd-archive` | committed export durable before it is advertised; may lag the live session by at most one checkpoint | | `project_code_memory` | project/code knowledge and observations (optional, deployment-selected) | deployment-defined (e.g. `chd-project`) | eventual; background sync permitted |
`coordination_report`, `control_key`, `session_archive`, and `project_code_memory` MUST be routed as separate logical classes. The first two share the controller namespace only because their authority and immediate consistency are the same; they retain distinct tool-class routing, grants, audits, and readback fields. A completion report or any coordination-critical record MUST be written to `coordination_report` on the controller path; a `project_code_memory` write MUST never be presented as the acknowledgement of a report. The namespace mapping is configuration (`storage.*` in VOL-D §1.10) and is readable via effective-routing readback; an implementation that routes coordination or control writes through a delayed sync path is non-conforming (VOLB-050). The archive class has its own writer (the archive ingestor, [VOL-F replacement map](VOL-F-reference-map.md) (historical section 2)), its own grants (VOL-C §8.8) and its own retention rules (§8); it is never the writer of coordination/control records, and no control record is duplicated into archive except the policy snapshot required for restore (§3.11).
---

## 2. Key normalization and layout
**VOLB-003 (key layout, canonical form).** Every DuckBrain key in this specification is normalized to the canonical leading-slash form (F-019: DuckBrain requires keys to start with `/`). The canonical key layout is:
| Canonical DuckBrain key | Writer | Content | |---|---|---| | `/chd/room/<room-id>/m<seq:012d>` | harness only | RoomMessage (§3.1) | | `/chd/room/<room-id>/_head` | harness only | SeqHead (§5.1) | | `/chd/registry/<agent-id>` | harness only | RegistryEntry (§3.2) | | `/chd/bond/<agent-id>/<bond-id>` | harness only | SessionBond (§3.3) | | `/chd/limits/<scope>` | harness only | LimitSet (§3.4) | | `/chd/send/<send-id>/manifest` | harness only | SendManifest (§3.5) | | `/chd/objective/<objective-id>` | harness only | ObjectiveRecord (§3.6) | | `/chd/assignment/<assignment-id>` | harness only | AssignmentRecord (§3.6) | | `/chd/delegation/<delegation-id>` | harness only | DelegationRecord (§3.6) | | `/chd/rule/<rule-id>` | harness only | StandingRule (§3.7) | | `/chd/acceptance/<objective-id>/<crit-id>` | harness only | AcceptanceCriterion (§3.8) | | `/chd/wait/<gate-id>` | harness only | Wait record (VOL-C §6.5, VOLC-047) | | `/chd/audit/<yyyymmddThhmmssZ>-<id>` | harness only | Audit record (VOL-C §8.6, VOLC-064) | | `/chd/aggregation/<send-id>` | harness only | Fan-out aggregation record (VOL-C §5.6, VOLC-032) | | `/chd/ticket/<ticket-id>` | controller ticket service (VOL-E) | TicketRecord (§3.14) | | `/chd/ticket/<ticket-id>/event/m<seq:012d>` | controller ticket service | Ticket transition event, ordered per ticket | | `/chd/report/<send-id>/<report-id>` | harness only | Report envelope + content descriptor (VOL-D §3.1) | | `/chd/dataset/<send-id>/<dataset-id>` | harness only | DatasetDescriptor (§3.10) | | `/chd/dataset/<send-id>/<dataset-id>/r<row:08d>` | harness only | One dataset row (§3.10) | | `/chd/grant/<grant-id>` | harness only | GrantRecord incl. meta-grant (§3.13) | | `/chd/policy/<session-id>/<snapshot-id>` | harness only | SessionPolicySnapshot (§3.11) | | `/chd/pattern/<pattern-id>` | harness (mirror) | AdvisoryLearnedPattern (§3.9) |
Archive namespace `chd-archive` (volume and grants per VOLD-044/D-018), checkpoint-scoped as of rev 2.1 (one ExportManifest per checkpoint, one SessionArchive index per session):
| Canonical key | Writer | Content | |---|---|---| | `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>` | archive ingestor | SessionArchive index (§3.12) — discovery entry for a replacement | | `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>/<checkpoint-id>/export.json` | archive ingestor | Native Hermes session export payload (§3.12) | | `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>/<checkpoint-id>/manifest` | archive ingestor | ExportManifest for that checkpoint (§3.12) | | `/sessions/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>/<checkpoint-id>/policy` | archive ingestor | SessionPolicySnapshot copy for restore (§3.11) | | `/gaps/<agent>/<profile>/<session-id>/<checkpoint-id>` | archive ingestor | ArchiveGapRecord — declared coverage gap or failed export (§3.12, VOLB-069) |
The archive namespace is written only by the archive ingestor using its own credential; the harness never writes it, and no agent holds a direct archive credential ([VOL-F replacement map](VOL-F-reference-map.md) (historical section 2.3)). Archive reads are grant-gated (VOL-C §8.8) and resolved through the lookup queries of §5.10.
Older DESIGN.md/DATA-MODEL.md rev 1.0 examples that show these families without the leading slash are superseded by this table; the normalization is mechanical and total (prepend `/`).
**VOLB-012 (key grammar).** Room message seq is zero-padded to 12 digits (`m000000000042`) so the lexicographic key order equals the numeric order in `GET /api/keys/flat` listings. Regexes enforced by the harness write gate (agents cannot write any `/chd/*` key directly; D9):
``` room message key: ^/chd/room/(obj|task|space)-[a-z0-9-]+/m[0-9]{12}$ bond key: ^/chd/bond/[a-z][a-z0-9-]*/b-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]+$ manifest key: ^/chd/send/s-[0-9]{8}-[0-9]{4}-[a-z0-9]+/manifest$ general: ^/chd/[a-z0-9_-]+(/[A-Za-z0-9._-]+)*$ ```
**VOLB-013 (no reserved-key collisions).** `_head` is the only reserved final segment under a room prefix; the write gate rejects any non-`_head` key whose final segment does not match `m[0-9]{12}`.

## 3. Logical record schemas
Conventions for every record: JSON content stored as the DuckBrain `content` string; `attributes` carry the indexed filter fields (D7); every record carries `schema_version` (int, §8), `rev` (int, writer-monotone per key, §4.2), and `ts` (RFC 3339 UTC, harness clock). Field types below are JSON types. Constraints are enforced by the harness on write; DuckBrain performs no validation (D2).

### 3.1 RoomMessage
One entry in a room's ordered log. Stored at `/chd/room/<room-id>/m<seq>`. Extends DATA-MODEL §1.4; amendments noted.
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `room` | string | matches room id grammar | Key family this seq belongs to | | `seq` | int | ≥ 1, allocated per §5.1, unique per room | Durable position in the room's total order | | `thread_root` | int \| null | null for room-level messages | Seq of the thread ROOT message (the original request). Set on every reply | | `reply_to` | int \| null | null, or an existing `seq` in this room | Immediate parent (RL-12 tree edge) | | `from` | string | `owner`, `vp/<surface-id>`, `signal:<source>`, or member agent id | Attribution | | `to` | string | agent id \| `group` \| `@<agent-id>` \| null | Wake routing only; never read scoping | | `kind` | enum | `msg \| question \| status \| directive \| task \| report \| incident` — the complete enum (R31-003); no other value validates | `question` = answer owed in-thread; `status` = progress/state post (incl. waiting-for-human notices); `directive` opens an objective; `task` opens a task/subthread; `report` carries the report attachment; `incident` is service-written only. Per-role/per-room legality is the single table in VOL-C §3.6 (VOLC-066) — this schema does not restate it | | `body` | string | non-empty | Human-readable text | | `attach` | object[] | optional | Report objects ride here for `kind=report` (RL-6) | | `dedupe_key` | string | optional, caller-chosen | Idempotent acceptance (§6.2); indexed in `attributes` | | `send_id` | string | optional; required for `kind=report` | The send this report answers; indexed in `attributes` | | `ts` | string | RFC 3339 UTC | Harness-observed write time (message time, not DuckBrain server time) |
`attributes` (for D7 attr filters): `{ "kind": <kind>, "from": <from>, "send_id": <send_id or "">, "dedupe_key": <dedupe_key or "">, "thread_root": <int or ""> }`.
Amendment vs DATA-MODEL §1.4: the ambiguous optional `thread` field is replaced by the explicit pair `thread_root` (stable grouping key for reads) and `reply_to` (tree edge); `dedupe_key` and `send_id` are promoted into attributes so the pending-send and dedupe queries (§5) are single prefix reads.
**VOLB-014.** A message is accepted only with a `seq` allocated by §5.1; the seq is part of the key and the content, and a message without a well-formed key/seq match is refused by the write gate.
**VOLB-015 (no self-echo, owner posting).** `from: owner` / `from: vp/*` messages are logged once; the harness MUST NOT compose a wake back to the VP surface for its own message (RL-6, DESIGN.md §11.3).

### 3.2 RegistryEntry
Responsibilities registry mirror (CT-09, RL-8). Config remains authoritative; the record is the readable mirror agents resolve "who owns X" from.
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `agent` | string | agent id | Subject | | `role` | enum | `director \| manager \| supervisor` | Role at mirror time | | `responsibility` | string | non-empty | "who owns X" | | `config_rev` | string | harness config generation hash | Which config generation this mirror reflects | | `ts` | string | RFC 3339 UTC | Mirror time |
**VOLB-016.** The harness rewrites every registry key on config load when `config_rev` changes; a registry read that returns a `config_rev` older than the loaded generation is served with a `stale_mirror: true` marker by the read API (§5.6) but never blocks a read.

### 3.3 SessionBond
The bond between one agent and one Hermes session in the context of one room and one work branch. Replaces DATA-MODEL §1.6's one-bond-per-agent shape and the earlier one-bond-per-(agent × room) shape: **a bond is per (agent, room, subthread_root, work_uid)** so one agent can hold several concurrent tasks in the same room, each with its own session, without mixing conversations (R31-022, D-025). Full identity contract in §7.
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `bond_id` | string | `b-YYYYMMDD-HHMM-<rand>` | Stable CHD identity of this bond | | `agent` | string | agent id | Owner | | `room` | string | room id the bond is attached to | Thread identity context (NOT a Hermes identity) | | `subthread_root` | int \| null | seq of the task/subthread root; null for room-level work | Which branch of the room this session serves (R31-022) | | `work_uid` | string \| null | ticket id, assignment id, or send id | The one work item this session owns; prevents two tasks sharing a session | | `generation` | int | ≥ 1, incremented on replacement | Distinguishes successive sessions for the same work item | | `parent_bond_id` | string \| null | existing bond id | Set when this session was provisioned by fork (§7.5) | | `fork_mode` | enum \| null | `preserve_parent_snapshot \| current_policy`; null for fresh sessions | Which D-038 policy produced this session (§3.11) | | `policy_snapshot_id` | string \| null | existing snapshot id | Effective permission snapshot bound to this session (VOLB-051) | | `policy_rev` | int \| null | ≥ 1; null until the snapshot is written | The snapshot revision this bond froze at creation; readback of a session returns exactly this revision's contents (VOL-C §8.3.1 VOLC-068b) and resync increments it atomically (§8.9) | | `hermes_base_url` | string | the gateway URL serving this session | Which Hermes instance owns the session | | `hermes_session_id` | string \| null | Hermes session id (`X-Hermes-Session-Id` value) | The session reference; null until first NEW delivery returns one | | `session_key` | string \| null | `X-Hermes-Session-Key` value scoped to this bond | Stable memory-scope key for the session (VOL-C §0/VOLC-022); null for NEW-mode bonds until the gateway echoes one | | `hermes_profile` | string | the named Hermes profile the session runs under | Profile-bound auth: authentication binds to the routed profile (hermes_gateway_check; VOLD-014 binding) | | `state` | enum | `provisioned \| active \| retired \| lost` | Lifecycle per §7.4 | | `runtime_caps` | object | capabilities snapshot from `GET /v1/capabilities` | What the serving Hermes advertised at bind time | | `reuse_policy` | enum | `reuse-until-wedged \| always-new` | CT-04 knob (unchanged) | | `ts` / `retired_ts` | string | RFC 3339 UTC | State times |
**VOLB-017.** A bond is keyed by `(agent, room, subthread_root, work_uid)`, with `generation` selecting the live one; the DuckBrain key carries `bond_id` so that a retired bond's record remains readable (audit) while the *current* bond for an identity tuple is resolved by highest `(generation, rev)` with `state ∈ {provisioned, active}` (version selection §4.2). Two tasks in one room assigned to one agent therefore hold two bonds with distinct `hermes_session_id`s; a reply or report is routed to the bond whose `subthread_root` owns the message's thread (§7.5). `max_sessions` bounds the number of simultaneously `active` bonds of one agent, not the number of rooms.
**VOLB-067 (concurrency fixture — R31-022 acceptance).** The fixture below is the normative proof that the bond key grammar admits **two concurrent tasks for the same agent in the same room**, each with a distinct bond id and a distinct thread (mirrored as the worked example in DATA-MODEL §1.6). Setup: supervisor `sup-nova` (max_sessions ≥ 2) is a member of task room `task-auth-14`; two `kind=task` messages opened two subthreads:
| # | bond key | agent | room | subthread_root | work_uid | gen | hermes_session_id | thread owned | state | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | `/chd/bond/sup-nova/b-20261109-0914-q4x7` | sup-nova | task-auth-14 | 42 | T-101 | 1 | `sess-aa11…` | replies under root 42 | active | | 2 | `/chd/bond/sup-nova/b-20261109-0917-m8k3` | sup-nova | task-auth-14 | 57 | T-205 | 1 | `sess-bb22…` | replies under root 57 | active |
Both bonds are simultaneously `active`; the identity tuples differ in `(subthread_root, work_uid)` only. A reply to message `m…042` is owned by bond 1 and delivered (REUSE) to `sess-aa11…`; a reply to `m…057` is owned by bond 2 and delivered to `sess-bb22…` — never the other way round (VOLB-063). The old one-bond-per-(agent × room) key could not express this state; that grammar is retired (R31-022). `capacity accounting` derives from the same identities: runnable queue = active bonds whose work item is runnable, capped by `max_sessions` (bonds) and `max_parallel.<kind>` (work items per room kind).

### 3.4 LimitSet
Typed caps (RL-14/RL-15, CT-13). Config is the authority; `/chd/limits/<scope>` is the readback mirror. One record per scope: `scope = "gateway:<gw-id>"`, `"type:<role>"`, or `"agent:<agent-id>"`.
| Field | Type | Constraint | Meaning | |---|---|---|---| | `scope` | string | one of the three forms above | What the cap gates | | `caps` | object | e.g. `{"max_inflight": 4}` / `{"max_parallel": {...}}` / `{"max_sessions": 2}` | Configured ceilings | | `config_rev` | string | generation hash | Mirror freshness marker |
**VOLB-018 (cap accounting is derived, not counted twice).** Runtime usage per scope is DERIVED from SendManifest states (§3.5): `usage(gateway) = # manifests in states {admitted, dispatched, await_report} with lease_expires_at > now`; `usage(agent) = # active bonds of that agent` (bounded by `max_sessions`). There is **no separate inflight counter record** — a derived count cannot drift from its evidence, and crash recovery of §6.4 re-derives it from manifests. Caps gate RUNNING only; scheduling/queuing is never refused for capacity (RL-15).
**VOLB-019 (cap read/update contract).** Reading effective caps and usage is the harness API `GET /v1/status` (ENDPOINTS §4.10) extended with, per scope, `{ "caps": {...}, "usage": N, "queued": M }`. "Update" of a cap is a **config change** through the operator-owned `harness.toml` path (R-001, N-2); agents cannot write `/chd/limits/*` (D9). A cap update activates on harness reload and is visible when `config_rev` advances.

### 3.5 SendManifest
One record per composed send; the durable heart of the crash-safe sequence (§6). Stored at `/chd/send/<send-id>/manifest`. Extends DATA-MODEL §2's one-line sketch into the full state machine.

## 4. Ordering and version rules (F-019)

### 4.1 Room order
**VOLB-005 (restated as requirement).** The durable total order of a room is the sequence of allocated `seq` values (§5.1). DuckBrain's timestamp/UUID ordering is NEVER used as room order. Readers sort fetched messages by `seq` client-side; the zero-padded key (VOLB-012) makes key listings agree with the same order.

### 4.2 Version selection for single-state keys
Manifests, bonds, objective/assignment/delegation/rule/criterion records are logically single-state but physically multi-version (D4). Rules:
**VOLB-025.** Every state-carrying record content carries integer `rev`, monotone per key, incremented by the harness on every transition. The **effective version** of a key is the fetched version with the highest `rev`. If multiple records have that highest `rev`, they are effective only when their canonical content bytes are identical; otherwise recovery rejects the key with `integrity_equal_rev_conflict`, records an incident, and pages the operator. Readers MUST resolve effective state this way and MUST NOT trust `GET /api/memories/key/:key` "latest-by-timestamp" (same-millisecond order is not durable, D4). A random-id tie-break is permitted only after byte-identity has been established for all equal-rev records.
**VOLB-026 (idempotent rewrites).** A writer retrying a transition MUST write the same `(rev, content)`; two versions with identical `(rev, content)` are tolerated and harmless. Writing different content at the same `rev` is refused by the harness's write gate.

### 4.3 Pagination / cursors
**VOLB-027.** All CHD list reads are **keyset-cursor reads, not offset pagination**: DuckBrain list ordering is `timestamp DESC, id ASC` (not write order), so offset windows shift under concurrent writes. Cursor = last observed `seq` (rooms) or last observed `rev`+ts (single-state keys). The harness over-fetches with `prefix` + `after` and filters client-side by the cursor.

### 4.4 Concurrency
**VOLB-010 (restated).** Exactly one harness instance writes `/chd/*` keys; all agent writes arrive through the harness API (§5). Cross-process concurrency on one namespace is therefore out of scope for this revision; the version-selection rules above remain the safety net for retry-duplicated writes (VOLB-025). **OPEN DESIGN WORK (OPEN-1):** multi-instance harness (active/passive or sharded-by-room) requires either a released DuckBrain CAS/declared-table surface or an external lease; not designed here.
**VOLB-066 (writer lease and restart exclusion).** The single writer is enforced by a durable writer lease at `/chd/system/writer` = `{writer_id, instance_id, boot_id, acquired_ts, heartbeat_ts, expires_ts}`. A starting harness takes the lease only if it is absent or expired; renews every `writer.heartbeat_s` (default 30); and refuses to serve (`503 writer_lease_held`) while another unexpired lease exists. Clock-skewed expiries are detected by requiring two consecutive failed heartbeats older than 2× the interval. Takeover requires a fresh `boot_id`, an atomic compare-and-set on the observed lease version, and a durable takeover incident; a stale owner may not write after losing that CAS. **Partition + expiry walkthrough:** H1 holds the lease and dispatches a run; the network partition prevents H1 heartbeats, so its lease appears expired to H2 while H1 may still execute remotely. H2's startup is refused unless the external lease authority confirms H1's lease is absent and the CAS succeeds; an expired timestamp alone is not proof that H1 stopped. If H2 cannot obtain that authority, it remains refused (`503 writer_lease_held_or_unknown`) and does not allocate a head, append a message, or release a capacity slot. This makes "two harnesses after a partition" a startup refusal rather than a silent double-write race.

## 5. Query / write contracts (F-006)
DuckBrain stores JSON memories; the **query/write semantics** below are supplied by the harness's own API (the only surface agents and VPs touch). Each contract names the DuckBrain reads/writes that implement it. All examples use canonical keys (§2).

### 5.1 Sequence allocation — atomic, crash-safe (F-007)
**Mechanism (single-writer, write-ahead window):**
1. The harness holds an in-process per-room allocator under a mutex. 2. When its reserved window is exhausted, it reserves the next block by writing the SeqHead record `/chd/room/<room-id>/_head` = `{ "next": base+BLOCK, "rev": r+1, "ts": ... }` (BLOCK default 64) and waits for the fsync ack (VOLB-011). 3. Each message allocation consumes one number from the window in memory — no additional write per allocation; the message write itself (§6.2) is the durable evidence of that seq.
**SeqHead record:** `{ "room": "<room-id>", "next": int, "rev": int, "reserved_from": int, "reserved_to": int, "writer_id": string, "ts": string }` at key `/chd/room/<room-id>/_head`, harness-only.
**Exact allocation and restart pseudocode (normative):**
```text allocate(room, request_id, canonical_message): assert writer_lease.owner == this_instance and writer_lease.not_expired lock(room_mutex) head = effective_record("/chd/room/" + room + "/_head") assert_equal_rev_contents_or_reject(head) if request_id is already indexed under /chd/room/<room>/dedupe/<request_id>: return the retained {message_key, seq, response}; if allocator[room] absent or allocator[room].next > allocator[room].reserved_to: base = head.next candidate = {next: base + BLOCK, reserved_from: base, reserved_to: base + BLOCK - 1, rev: head.rev + 1, writer_id: this_instance, ts: now} fsync_write_same_key(candidate) # retain old head as history allocator[room] = candidate seq = allocator[room].next; allocator[room].next += 1 message = canonical_message + {seq, request_id} fsync_write_once(/chd/room/<room>/m<seq>, message) fsync_write_once(/chd/room/<room>/dedupe/<request_id>, {message_key, seq, response}) return retained response
recover(room): require writer_lease_acquired_or_refuse_startup() head = effective_record(/chd/room/<room>/_head) messages = list_prefix(/chd/room/<room>/m*) assert_equal_rev_contents_or_reject(head, messages) max_seq = max(seq(message) for message in messages, default=-1) next_seq = max(head.next, max_seq + 1) candidate = {next: next_seq + BLOCK, reserved_from: next_seq, reserved_to: next_seq + BLOCK - 1, rev: head.rev + 1, writer_id: this_instance, ts: now} fsync_write_same_key(candidate) allocator[room] = candidate # Never reclaim the reserved tail; every gap remains permanent.
recover_send(send_id): versions = list_prefix(/chd/send/<send_id>/manifest) manifest = effective_record_or_reject_equal_rev(versions) reports = list_reports(send_id, attempt_id=manifest.attempt_id) attempts = list_prefix(/chd/send/<send_id>/attempt/) return canonical_manifest_with_attempts_reports(manifest, attempts, reports) ```
Every `fsync_write_once` is keyed by the record's stable key plus its caller idempotency key; a retry with the same key and canonical bytes returns the retained record, while changed bytes are rejected. No recovery step is permitted to say only “re-derive”: it names its prefix/query and retained input above.
**VOLB-028.** Seq MUST NOT be reused after a crash: restart recovery sets `next = max(max observed message seq in the family, last durable `_head`.next - 1) + 1`. Gaps are legal; duplicates are not. The in-process mutex + single writer guarantee no two allocations race (VOLB-010). This resolves DESIGN UQ-7/OQ-14 by selecting the falsifier's named fallback: the harness allocates seq through a single writer and agents POST through it (amending CT-05, VOLB-020).
**VOLB-058 (retained head reservations, R31-007).** The `_head` record is never deleted and is never rolled back: it retains `next` (the end of the last reserved block), `rev`, `reserved_from`, `reserved_to`, `writer_id` and `ts`. A restarted harness:
1. reads `_head` and the highest observed message key per room; 2. sets `next = max(observed_max + 1, head.next)` — never below a previously advertised reservation, so a number handed out before the crash cannot be reissued; 3. writes a new `_head` with `reserved_from = next`, `reserved_to = next + BLOCK - 1` and `rev + 1` **before** consuming any number from the window; 4. refuses to start if two live processes claim the same `writer_id`/lease (restart exclusion, §4.4), because two windows would otherwise interleave.
The reserved-but-unused tail is a legal gap forever; reclamation of that gap is forbidden (it would reuse numbers). The write gate rejects any message whose key falls inside a reserved window that the current writer did not allocate.
**VOLB-059 (canonical message and manifest recovery, R31-007).** Recovery reads the *canonical* records, never a derived cache: room messages by key prefix sorted by `seq`; manifests by effective `rev` (§4.2); bonds by `(generation, rev)`. If two versions of one key carry the **same `rev` but different content**, the harness does not pick a winner: it refuses the room with `500 integrity_equal_rev_conflict`, records an incident and pages the operator. Random-UUID tie-breaks are legal only when content is byte-identical (VOLB-025/026); a content disagreement is data corruption, not a race to be arbitrated.
**VOLB-020 (CT-05 amendment).** Agents do NOT hold DuckBrain write tokens for `/chd/*`. The sending "session" posts through harness endpoints (ENDPOINTS §4.2/§4.3 with an *agent* credential — the §6 matrix is amended: room post/reply/report are allowed to internal agents for rooms they are members of; all other endpoints remain agent-denied). The harness validates membership (DESIGN.md §4.6 read/post scoping) and is the only DuckBrain writer.

### 5.2 Ordered room read
`GET /v1/rooms/{room}/messages?since=<seq>&thread=<root_seq>&limit=<n>` (ENDPOINTS §4.7, contract notation). Implementation: DuckBrain `GET /api/memories?namespace=chd&prefix=/chd/room/<room-id>/&limit=500` (+ repeat pages by cursor per VOLB-027), filter `seq > since` (and `thread_root == thread` if given), sort ascending by `seq`, truncate to `limit`, return `next_since`.
Request/result example:
``` GET /v1/rooms/obj-fleet/messages?since=41&limit=100 → 200 { "room": "obj-fleet", "messages": [ { "seq": 42, "from": "director", "to": "group", "kind": "directive", "thread_root": null, "reply_to": null, "body": "...", "ts": "..." } ], "next_since": 42 } ```
**VOLB-029.** Results are always ascending by `seq`; a reader resuming from `next_since` sees no gaps and no duplicates. Thread reads (`?thread=<root_seq>`) return the subtree in `seq` order regardless of nesting depth (walk `reply_to` client-side to reconstruct the tree — DuckBrain has no join).

### 5.4 Fresh-report lookup
`GET /v1/sends/{send_id}/reports` and the verify loop's own read. Implementation: DuckBrain `GET /api/memories?namespace=chd&prefix=/chd/room/<room>/&attr.kind=report&attr.send_id=<send_id>` — attribute filters narrow the candidate set; the harness then applies the single V3 precedence in VOL-D §3.3 using `ingest_ts` against the matching attempt's `dispatch_ts`. The query returns candidates plus `stale_seen`, `duplicate_seen`, and the chosen `report_ref`; no DuckBrain table API is assumed.
The old CHD-3 `report.ts > request.timestamp` and the prior `report.ts >= dispatch_ts` wording are superseded. Agent timestamps and content timestamps are not query clocks; the service's persisted ingress timestamp is the trusted time.
``` → 200 { "send_id": "s-20261108-1015-k4m8", "fresh_reports": [ { "room": "task-crier-42", "seq": 87, "message_key": "/chd/room/task-crier-42/m000000000087", "status": "done", "ts": "..." } ], "stale_seen": 1 } ```
**VOLB-031.** A report whose correlation matches but whose harness `ingest_ts` precedes `dispatch_ts` for its `attempt_id` is returned in `stale_seen` and never closes a send (R-031). A report for a different `send_id`, `attempt_id`, or `session_ref` — however fresh — cannot close this send; correlation mismatch is reported as `wrong_request` or `attempt_mismatch`.
**VOLB-056 (freshness rule v3, R31-011; supersedes v2).** VOLD-025/VOLD-026 in VOL-D §3.2–§3.3 are the single authority for freshness and duplicate/late precedence. The trusted basis is harness-recorded `ingest_ts` compared with `dispatch_ts` for the same `(send_id, attempt_id, session_ref)`; agent and attachment timestamps are evidence only. The exact first-match table is not repeated here, preventing a second rule from drifting. A stale attachment in a newly accepted envelope is handled only by director acceptance review, while mismatched attempt/session can never close work.
**Stale attachment rule.** A report envelope posted now may carry content whose own timestamp is old (an attached log, an old artifact). Freshness is decided by the *envelope's* ingest time against the attempt's dispatch time; the content's own timestamps are evidence metadata evaluated by the director's acceptance review (VOLD-034), never by the send-closure test. This removes the "old attachment in a new envelope" ambiguity.
**VOLB-057 (attempt identity, R31-004).** Four identities are distinct and never substituted:
- **logical send** (`send_id`) — one owed piece of work; survives retries, fresh sessions and wait-resumes; - **attempt** (`attempt_id`, `attempt`) — one dispatch episode against one target session; a ladder rung that changes the session, and every wait-resume, mints a new attempt; - **gateway request key** (`gateway_request_key`) — the `Idempotency-Key` of exactly one POST.
**Identity and rotation table (normative).** These identifiers are distinct; none may be substituted for another:
| Identity | Scope and durability | Rotation rule | What it correlates | |---|---|---|---| | `send_id` (logical send) | One owed piece of work; durable for the obligation | Never rotates across retries, NEW/REUSE changes, deleted sessions, or wait-resumes | The request message, all attempts, reports, and the final send outcome | | `attempt_id` (attempt ordinal) | One dispatch episode against one session-target | Mint exactly once for each new target or wait-resume; never reopen or reuse a closed attempt | One report, one run reference, and one capacity hold | | `gateway_request_key` | One gateway POST idempotency key | Reuse only when `attempt_id` and the complete session-target are unchanged; rotate with every new attempt | One POST and its gateway admission/run result | | `session_target` | Immutable `{gateway_id, session_id, agent_id, mode, bond_generation}` snapshot | Never mutate in place; a new session, deleted session, new bond generation, or target conflict creates a new snapshot and therefore a new attempt | The exact external target to which the gateway request was sent |
The gateway request key is derived from `(send_id, attempt_id, session_target_digest)` and is persisted before the POST. The harness rejects a key whose stored target snapshot differs from the requested target (`422 attempt_target_conflict`). A response loss, transport timeout, or failed POST is **unknown execution**, not proof that no work ran; the harness MUST reconcile the stored run/admission reference before any external-effect retry. The supported Hermes behavior is only the capability-probed contract in §7.2: an unchanged-target retry may replay or return a conflict, while a new target requires a new key. CHD does not claim universal replay-or-conflict semantics.
| Retry situation | Required action | External-effect authority | |---|---|---| | Response lost after POST | Query run status, then resolve unknown with `admission_id` + `execution_generation`; if still unknown, hold slot and page. Do not POST another attempt | Send orchestrator after reconciliation only | | Retry to the same target | Reuse the same `attempt_id`, target snapshot, and key; accept replay or conflict and reconcile the original run | Send orchestrator; no fresh effect until original outcome is known | | Ladder rung selects a fresh `NEW` session | Persist the new target snapshot and successor `attempt_id`/key; link `supersedes_attempt_id`; do not reuse the old key | Director/send orchestrator decision recorded with rung evidence | | Target session deleted | Record `target_deleted`; query session history/run status; mint a successor only when the old attempt is proven stopped or an authorized unknown-execution decision is recorded | Director or delegated send owner; never automatic blind replay | | Gateway returns unknown/ambiguous result | Classify `unknown`, keep capacity held, run bounded reconciliation; only an explicit authorized decision may retry an external effect | Director authority record plus send orchestrator execution |

**VOLB-070 (restore procedure — ordered, validated, explicitly limited).** Restoring a session from the archive onto a replacement host is this procedure, in order; a step that fails stops the procedure with a recorded restore-incident (never a degraded "best effort" import):
1. **Discover** — run QA-1 under a resolvable archive read grant; select the SessionArchive of the target session. 2. **Select** — run QA-2; take the latest `state=committed` ExportManifest. If none exists (all failed/gaps), stop: `restore_failed{reason: no_committed_manifest}` with the gap records attached. 3. **Verify integrity** — fetch the payload; recompute sha256 and compare to `payload_digest`. Resolve the replacement from current permissions before activation, even when the archived snapshot is present. Record `restore_decision: current_policy`, the source checkpoint and source policy revision when present; when the source revision is absent, record `null` plus a verified reason. Record the newly effective current policy revision. A `snapshot_missing` marker describes historical coverage only and never changes the current-policy decision. (VOLC-069; D-039 supersedes VOLD-063.) 7. **Record the checkpoint** — the new bond (new `generation`, `parent_bond_id` of the retired bond) records `imported_checkpoint_id/seq` and the archive identity it came from; delayed messages for the old generation follow VOLB-064 (`routed_to: retired_generation`). 8. **Report** — the restore emits a report stating `completeness`, the coverage window, every open gap (QA-4), and the new session/bond ids.
**Limitation (normative):** this procedure CANNOT restore a live session. It populates a new local session store from committed exports; it does not resume the archived session, does not reuse its session id, and does not reconstruct conversation prompts (R-019). ### 5.12 Dataset query contracts (R31-030)
CHD uses logical `ReportDataset` and `ReportRow` records persisted as JSON memories in DuckBrain; it does not require or imply DuckBrain's unreleased declared-table API. The service owns all reads and writes, enforces the report's authorization, and maps these records to the keys in §3.10.
`GET /v1/reports/{report_id}/dataset` returns only a published dataset when the caller has report-read permission for the linked room/send and the dataset's retention window has not expired. A caller without permission receives the existing indistinguishable `404 not_found`; no row existence is disclosed.
Query parameters are `filter` (a closed, typed expression over declared column names), `order_by` (declared column plus `ASC|DESC`), `page_size` (1..500), and `cursor` (opaque keyset cursor). The service validates filter names/types, orders deterministically by `order_by` plus `row_id`, returns `{dataset_id, columns, rows, next_cursor, has_more}`, and rejects unknown columns or invalid operators as `422 dataset_query_invalid`. Offset pagination is not supported. Rows are keyed by harness-assigned dense `row_id` (`r00000001` onward), unique within a dataset and immutable; `values` must match the declared typed columns.
**VOLB-073 (atomic dataset publish and retry).** A report and its dataset are written through one harness transaction boundary: descriptor and rows remain `staging`, and neither the report nor any row is readable until every row has validated, the expected `row_count` matches, and the descriptor flips to `published`. Validation failure is named `422 schema_validation` (or `422 dataset_row_invalid` for a typed row); it leaves no readable report and records the audit failure. A retry with the same `(send_id, attempt_id, content_digest)` is the exact replay row in VOL-D §3.3; a different digest is the second-report row, never an in-place update. Corrections publish a new `dataset_id` and report. Retention/tombstoning follows §8 and preserves the report-to-dataset linkage in the audit record.

## 6. Crash-safe sequences (F-007)
All writes are harness-mediated, `fsync`-durability acked (VOLB-011), and idempotent under the stated dedupe keys. Time origin for every comparison is the harness clock; DuckBrain's persisted write `timestamp` (201 body, DB-GAP-045) is audit evidence, never a clock source.

### 6.1 The canonical sequence (happy path)
**Actor/trigger/read/check/write/evidence.** The harness triggers S1 when the orchestrator decides to send. It reads the room message and current manifest, checks the dedupe key and cap, writes each durable manifest revision before the next external effect, and records the scheduler admission and gateway response. Evidence is the fsync acknowledgement plus matching `send_id`, `attempt_id`, and `run_ref`. Normal example: the manifest moves `composed → queued → admitted → dispatched`, then the correlated report moves it to `verified`. Failure example: the gateway response is lost after POST; the harness reads the stored attempt, does not assume failure, and uses [reconcile](terminology.md#reconcile) with the same identity; an unknown result holds capacity.
**S1 compose.** Orchestrator decides to wake agent A in room R for message seq N: write SendManifest `state=composed` (dedupe: `send_id` minted once; a crash here leaves a composed manifest that restart recovery either dispatches or cancels — never loses the request, because the request message itself is already durable).
**S2 admission reservation.** Check caps (VOLB-018/019). Under cap: transition `composed → queued` (manifest write), then request scheduler admission (bump, FACT-14 / CT-03). Scheduler-granted: `→ admitted` (+ `lease_expires_at = now + lease`, lease default 2× `stale_after_s`). Over cap: manifest stays `queued`-preceded (`composed`) and the send queues (RL-15 — scheduling never refused). **OPEN DESIGN WORK (OPEN-2):** bump semantics admit-once vs frequency (DESIGN UQ-3/Q-6); S2 is written against the wake_once resolution and needs no change if bump proves admit-once.
**S3 gateway delivery.** `admitted → dispatched`: the harness POSTs to the Hermes gateway per §7 (mode NEW or REUSE), records `dispatch_ts`, `run_ref` (from the response — Chat Completions echoes the explicit session id; Runs API returns `run_id`), `deadline_ts`. Write ack before the harness reports the send as dispatched anywhere.
**S4 agent work + report.** The agent session posts `kind=report` with `send_id` through the harness (§5.1/VOLB-020); the message write acks (fsync), then the harness may wake the parent (CT-07).
**S5 report linking.** Verify loop finds the report (§5.4), validates (CT-06: schema, freshness, artifacts), writes `report_ref` + `state=await_report` (report received, verification pending).
**S6 ack/verify close.** Verdict `verified` → manifest `state=verified` (terminal); cap release is implicit (usage re-derivation, VOLB-018). Verdict paths follow §5.1 DESIGN ladder, each rung appended to `rung_history`.

### 6.2 Idempotent message acceptance
**Actor/trigger/read/check/write/evidence.** The harness triggers acceptance on each room-message, report, or manifest write. It reads the target prefix by `dedupe_key`, checks whether the retained body is byte-identical, writes only on a miss, and returns the retained record on a replay. Evidence is `200` with the original key/sequence for an exact replay. Normal example: retrying the same report returns the original response and creates no second message. Failure example: the same key carries different bytes; the harness writes no new record, returns `409 duplicate`, and records the conflict for audit.
**VOLB-032.** Every accepting write (room message, report, manifest transition) carries a caller-supplied `dedupe_key`. Acceptance algorithm: (1) attribute-filtered read for `attr.dedupe_key=<k>` under the target prefix (§5.4-style); (2) hit → return the original response (`200`, not `201`), write nothing; (3) miss → allocate, write, ack; the dedupe fields live in the record itself (no second write). A replay with the same `dedupe_key` and a *different* body is `409 duplicate` (ENDPOINTS §5).

### 6.3 Duplicate and late delivery
**Actor/trigger/read/check/write/evidence.** The harness triggers this check when a gateway retry or late report arrives. It reads the stored idempotency key, target snapshot, dispatch timestamp, and report correlation, checks identity before freshness, and writes either a retained replay or a late/stale annotation. Evidence is the original run reference and a durable `late_report` or `bad_report` record. Normal example: a fresh report for the original attempt links once and closes only the current open outcome. Failure example: a stale or wrong-request report is rejected even when its envelope timestamp is fresh; the harness writes the reason and does not reopen an escalated send.
**VOLB-033 (duplicates).** A duplicated gateway POST (network retry after Hermes admitted the first) is absorbed by the Hermes Idempotency-Key (§7.2 — canonical mode replays the original answer; a changed identity is `409 admission_conflict` and nothing runs). CHD never re-POSTs with a changed identity under the same key; the send's `run_ref` correlates retries.
**VOLB-034 (late delivery).** A report arriving after `deadline_ts` but fresh and valid is still linked (`report_ref`) and the manifest records `late_report: true`, but the ladder outcome already taken (escalated) stands; the incident is annotated, not auto-reverted. A *stale* report (`ts < dispatch_ts`) is never linked (VOLB-031).

### 6.4 Restart recovery
**Actor/trigger/read/check/write/evidence.** On startup the harness triggers recovery before accepting new sends. It reads room heads, open manifests, run references, leases, datasets, and bonds; checks each state against its allowed recovery operation; writes repaired projections and audit revisions; and then admits new work. Normal example: an open `queued` manifest is [re-drive](terminology.md#re-drive)d with its persisted admission key and no duplicate charge. Failure example: an expired lease has no terminal remote evidence; the harness [reconcile](terminology.md#reconcile)s, records `uncertain`, keeps the slot held, and pages at the bound rather than releasing it.
**VOLB-035.** On startup the harness MUST run, before accepting new sends: (a) R2 head re-derivation for every room (VOLB-028/058); (b) R1 pending-sends scan; for each open manifest: `composed/queued/admitted` → re-drive S2/S3 using the persisted transition/admission keys and the unchanged target; `dispatched` with `run_ref` → query the run status (§6.7); (c) R3 lease-expiry scan → reconcile, never "release because time passed" (VOLB-061); (d) dataset recovery: any `staging` dataset is marked `failed` (VOLB-050); (e) bond recovery: bonds whose `hermes_session_id` no longer exists are marked `lost` and their open sends re-attempt as a new attempt (§6.7).
**VOLB-060 (run-status reconciliation, R31-006).** For every dispatched attempt the harness asks, in this order, until it gets a definitive answer or exhausts the bound:
1. `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` (or the session-history equivalent) → `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `interrupted`; 2. `POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/resolve-unknown` with the stored `admission_id` + `execution_generation` → definitive outcome or `unknown`; 3. session history `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` — the presence of the agent's report turn is positive evidence the attempt executed.
**Run-status decision table (the owner and probe are normative):**
| Observed status | Reconciliation owner | Check method | Slot may release? | |---|---|---|---| | `running` / `proven-running` | send orchestrator | run GET says running, or an execution heartbeat is newer than the probe start | **No**; renew/hold the lease | | `stopped` / `completed` / `failed` / `cancelled` / `interrupted` / terminal report | send orchestrator | terminal run GET or correlated terminal report, with `run_id` + `attempt_id` match | **Yes**, after durable terminal manifest write | | `unreachable` | recovery operator on behalf of service writer | bounded retries of run GET, resolve-unknown, then session history; transport remains unavailable | **No**; unreachable is not proof of stop | | `unknown` | service writer, then director at the bound | resolve-unknown returns unknown or identities cannot be reconciled | **No**; explicitly forbidden without stop confirmation |
Outcomes are classified **proven-stopped**, **proven-running**, **uncertain**, or **unreachable**. `proven-stopped` (terminal run status, or a terminal report) is the only outcome that releases the slot. `uncertain` keeps `paused:uncertain` with the slot held, retries the probe with bounded backoff, and pages the operator at the bound. `unreachable` keeps `paused:unreachable` and holds the slot; it is **not** a release trigger. If the harness itself stays unavailable past `capacity.unresolved_hold_s` (EXPLICIT-DEFAULT 7200), the recovery operator owns the reconciliation and may only release after a run-status probe proves termination (or an explicit operator attestation is recorded as an audit decision that is the configured emergency authority); lease expiry alone never qualifies. The service writer resumes the held scan when it returns. This separates bounded detection from proven slot reclamation.

### 6.6 Report linking + ack ordering
**VOLB-037.** Order is always: DuckBrain write ack (fsync) → then any wake, notification, or 2xx to an external caller. No harness response may promise a state that is not yet durably acked; the reverse (durably acked, response lost) is safe by dedupe. This is the "append acknowledgement" answer to F-019's durability question: **the ack IS the fsync'd DuckBrain append**; git history (~30 s debounce) and optional S3 push are downstream transports with their own RPO, never the ack (VOLB-007). The harness additionally verifies `X-Durability == fsync` on every ack and treats a `buffered`-achieved ack on `chd` as a hard error (VOLB-011).

### 6.7 Cap release
**VOLB-038.** Usage counts derive from manifest states (VOLB-018); release happens on a terminal transition or on a *proven* stop (VOLB-060). A crashed harness releases nothing until restart reconciliation runs.
**VOLB-061 (expiry is detection, not proof — R31-006).** `lease_expires_at` is a **detection deadline**, not a reclamation licence. Policy:
1. A lease reaching expiry moves the attempt to `paused:uncertain` and emits `capacity_lease_expired{send_id}` — the slot stays charged. 2. The harness runs run-status reconciliation (VOLB-060). Only `proven-stopped` transitions the attempt terminal and frees the slot. 3. `uncertain` holds the slot and retries the probe at bounded backoff (`capacity.probe_backoff_s`, default 60 s, jittered, capped at 15 min) until `capacity.unresolved_hold_s`. 4. `unreachable` also holds the slot; a gateway outage therefore reduces available capacity instead of admitting a second run above the cap. 5. After the hold bound the operator path is the ONLY release (VOLB-060 last paragraph). The system prefers refusing new work to admitting a run it cannot prove stopped.
Consequence, stated plainly: partition + expired lease NEVER admits a second run above `max_inflight`/`max_sessions` while the first may still be executing. Availability is sacrificed before the cap is. A queued send whose blocking cap frees is dispatched by the next cycle or by the wake-on-reply path; queuing never expires the underlying request message, only the send (`stale_after` → `deferred`, counted, superseded next cycle).

## 7. Session identity (F-010)

### 7.1 The two identities
**VOLB-039.** Thread identity = (room, seq/thread tree) in DuckBrain. Hermes session identity = the session id minted by Hermes' API server, referenced by the bond (§3.3). CHD NEVER synthesizes conversation content into a prompt (RL-3/R-019): the only conversation carriers are (a) a NEW session's first-turn message and (b) a REUSE session's next turn. All shared context lives in rooms, which agents read themselves via the room-read tool (§5.2) — an agent tool action, never harness prompt-reconstruction (§4.1 DESIGN).

### 7.2 Mapping NEW/REUSE onto existing Hermes APIs
Hermes API server (OpenAI-compatible; bearer auth) exposes: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (session continuity via explicit `X-Hermes-Session-Id` header; without it the session is derived from system prompt + first user message), `POST /api/sessions/{session_id}/chat[.stream]` (continue an existing session by id), `POST /v1/runs` + run controls (`/status`, `/stop`, `/approval`, `/resolve-unknown`), `Idempotency-Key` support with durable admission identity in canonical mode, `GET /v1/capabilities` for feature discovery, and `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages`. Session ids of deleted sessions are never remapped (`not_found`), and compressed sessions keep their id. Three further verified `hermes_gateway_check` facts are load-bearing here (review-log, official docs, fetched 2026-11-08):
- **REST session lifecycle**: creation, continuation, metadata/history, and **forks** are all provided by Hermes. CHD uses create + continue + history for **delivery** (NEW/REUSE), and uses **fork** for **session provisioning** of a task subthread: a manager's task assignment may fork the manager's session so the worker session starts with the parent context that the fork captures (D-025, [VOL-F replacement map](VOL-F-reference-map.md) (historical section 5)). Fork is never a delivery mode: the wake that delivers the assignment still runs as NEW on the forked session (VOL-C §4.1). An agent also MAY fork its own session inside Hermes-owned session semantics; that remains platform behavior outside CHD's contracts. - **Named profile routing binds authentication to the routed profile**: a bond's gateway calls therefore run under the agent's bound profile (`hermes_profile`, §3.3; VOLD-014 requires one profile per agent), which is what makes per-agent tool policy and credentials attributable at the gateway. - **Memory snapshots are frozen at session start** (documented Hermes behavior): a continued (REUSE) session does not observe memory or standing-rule changes made after its session started. Consequence: effective-rule evidence (§3.7, VOLB-022) must be read at session start or from a NEW session's readback; no propagation guarantee is assumed (D-013, Q-005).
**VOLB-040 (NEW).** Mode NEW = `POST /v1/chat/completions` **without** `X-Hermes-Session-Id`, with header `Idempotency-Key: <send_id>` and body carrying the composed directive as the sole user message plus the agent's configured system prompt/profile identity. The response echoes the created session id; the harness writes it into the bond (`hermes_session_id`, state `active`). A NEW rung of the ladder uses the same call with the fresh-obligation prompt (CT-06).
**VOLB-041 (REUSE).** Mode REUSE = `POST /v1/chat/completions` **with** `X-Hermes-Session-Id: <bond.hermes_session_id>` and the same Idempotency-Key rule. Equivalently `POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat` for stream-attached deliveries; the contract surface (headers, identity, idempotency semantics) is identical. Detached delegation results (if the harness uses runs) are read back via `GET /api/sessions/{id}/messages` — read, never replayed into a prompt.
**VOLB-042 (bond identity + endpoint/header/response contract).** The bond record (§3.3) is the durable join between thread identity and session identity. The response chain the harness MUST persist per send: session id (echoed), run_id / admission_id (Runs mode) → `run_ref`. Two simultaneous objectives for one agent hold two bonds (different rooms, different `hermes_session_id`s, both within `max_sessions`) — conversations cannot mix because Hermes scopes history by session id and CHD scopes wakes by bond.
**VOLB-043 (supported runtime version).** The serving Hermes gateway MUST present, at `GET /v1/capabilities`, `auth.required == true`, session continuity (explicit `X-Hermes-Session-Id` echo), and the `Idempotency-Key` canonical-mode behavior. The harness checks this at gateway onboarding and on every bond creation; a gateway failing the check gets `mode = always-new` bonds and a loud operator warning — REUSE is refused, not degraded silently. **OPEN DESIGN WORK (OPEN-3):** the minimum Hermes release number pinning the canonical-session-authority behaviors cited here; until verified, the capability probe (not a version number) is the gate.

### 7.3 NEW vs REUSE selection (single authority: VOL-C §4)
Per D-014 and the handoff ("map exactly which events choose NEW versus REUSE"), the **single normative decision table is VOL-C §4 (W1–W11, VOLC-021)** — session mapping is part of VOL-C's tool/delivery surface, and its table is the more complete one (it adds scheduler fire, reassignment, and temporary-agent rows). This volume does not duplicate it.
Binding notes for the VOL-B record contracts:
- **VOLB-044.** VOL-C's table is the single NEW/REUSE authority; `reuse_policy` can only force REUSE→NEW, never NEW→REUSE. The chosen mode is recorded on the send manifest (`mode`), and the session identity it produces is written to the bond (§3.3). Rev-1.0 of this volume carried its own eight-row table; it was superseded in integration by VOL-C §4 — the one behavioral difference (scheduled trigger fire: this volume's draft said "REUSE if active bond", VOL-C pins **NEW** per D-014's user description "scheduler invocations start new sessions") is resolved in VOL-C's favor (Q-007 anchor: user description governs; replies/follow-ups continue bonded sessions). - The REUSE mechanics (headers, session key, idempotency) are VOLB-041 and VOLC-022 — identical contracts, two views.

### 7.4 Lost / retired sessions and conflicts
**VOLB-045 (retired session).** A Hermes session id, once its session is deleted, is never remapped and answers `not_found`. On any REUSE delivery answered `404 not_found` (or a definitive session-missing error), the harness: marks the bond `retired` (write, fsync), posts a `kind=status` room message recording the loss, allocates a fresh bond, and delivers the pending message in NEW mode. The thread log (not the session) carries continuity — this is why lost sessions cost a context read, not a reconstruction.
**VOLB-045a (existing-versus-future classification, D-038).** The following table is normative and is the shared classification CHD31-06 MUST cite for its snapshot records; it does not duplicate CHD31-06's GrantRecord schema:
| Event | Session classification | Policy/snapshot outcome | |---|---|---| | Fork | **Future child session** at the fork boundary | `preserve_parent_snapshot` copies the parent snapshot; `current_policy` resolves current policy | | Restart / REUSE | **Existing session** (same Hermes session id and bond generation) | Retains its snapshot; in-flight operations keep the revision at their authorization boundary | | Replacement after loss/wedge | **Future replacement session** (new generation and session id) | Resolves `current_policy` before activation; archived snapshot is history; missing source snapshot records `snapshot_missing` without changing the decision | | Restore from archive | **Future imported session** (fresh local id; archived session is not resumed) | Resolves `current_policy` before activation; checkpoint snapshot is retained as history; absent source snapshot records `snapshot_missing` only |
A retired or lost session remains readable for audit but cannot authorize new work. A replacement or restore never silently inherits a live session id. See VOL-C §8.9 and VOL-D §1.11 for operation timing and resync authorization; CHD31-06 owns the lineage record details.
**VOLB-046 (conflicts).** `409 admission_conflict` on an Idempotency-Key retry means the key already names other work: treat as in-flight — poll `GET /v1/runs/{run_id}` instead of re-POSTing; never mint a new key for the same send (that would risk double execution). `409 unknown_execution` (Responses path) or run status `unknown` after an authority restart → `POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/resolve-unknown` with the stored `admission_id` + `execution_generation` from `run_ref`, reconcile outcome `interrupted`, re-enter the ladder at rung 0.
**VOLB-047 (runtime version skew).** Bond `runtime_caps` records the capabilities snapshot at bind time; on capability regression (gateway returns different features), existing REUSE bonds continue if the probe still passes, else follow VOLB-045's retired path. Hermes owns compaction/lifecycle (session ids survive compression — keep sending the same id); CHD stores no session content and runs no session store.

### 7.5 Fork provisioning, subthread routing, and roll-up (R31-022, D-025, D-038)
**VOLB-062 (task subthread provisioning).** A `kind=task` message that assigns a work unit creates a subthread (the message is `thread_root` for its replies) and a **provisioning decision**:
| Situation | Provisioning | Delivery | |---|---|---| | new work unit, no useful parent context | fresh session (`POST /v1/chat/completions`, continuation-less) | NEW | | new work unit that must inherit the assigner's working context | **fork** of the assigner's session at a named `fork_point_seq` | NEW (on the forked session) | | same work unit, further turn | existing bond | REUSE |
`fork_point_seq` is the last room message the parent session had observed when the assignment was composed; it is recorded on the bond so the child's context is auditable. The fork request is `POST /api/sessions/{parent_session_id}/fork` with `{fork_point_seq, policy_mode}`; the response's new session id is written to the child bond with `parent_bond_id`, `fork_mode`, `generation=1` and a fresh `SessionPolicySnapshot` (§3.11).
**VOLB-063 (which session owns a reply).** A reply or report posted into a thread is attributed to the bond whose `(room, subthread_root, work_uid)` matches the message's thread root. If no bond matches and the poster is a member, the message is still stored (audit) but it wakes no one and the poster receives `409 thread_not_owned` in the tool result, so a delayed response cannot silently attach itself to the wrong branch. A report whose `send_id` names an attempt of a different bond is `bad_report{reason: send_mismatch}` (VOL-D §3.3).
**VOLB-064 (generation and replacement).** When a session is lost, wedged or restored, the bond is superseded: `generation` increments, the old bond keeps `state=retired|lost`, and the new bond records `parent_bond_id` (null for a replacement, not a fork) plus the restore checkpoint if any ([VOL-F replacement map](VOL-F-reference-map.md) (historical section 6)). Delayed replies arriving for the retired generation are stored and flagged `routed_to: retired_generation`, never delivered into the new session; the harness's roll-up reads them from the room log.
**VOLB-065 (roll-up).** A manager's review of a child subthread produces one report in the parent thread whose `artifacts` include `child_report_refs[]` and whose `summary` states the aggregation result. Roll-up is a summary with cited child evidence; it never re-reads or re-injects the child transcript (D-017). The aggregation record (VOL-C §5.6) and the parent report are linked by `send_id` of the parent, so a reader can walk parent → aggregate → children without parsing prose.

## 8. Migration and retention
**VOLB-048 (schema migration).** Every record carries `schema_version` (this document = **3**; rev-1.1 records = 2; DATA-MODEL rev 1.0 records = 1). Version 3 adds: `attempt_id`/`attempt`/`gateway_request_key` on manifests, the bond subthread fields, `ReportEnvelope`/`DatasetDescriptor`/`DatasetRow`, `SessionPolicySnapshot`, `SessionArchive`/`ExportManifest`/`ArchiveGapRecord` (§3.12), `GrantRecord`, `TicketRecord`, and the `question` message kind. Migration is lazy: on read, an older record is upgraded in memory; on the record's next write it is persisted at the current version. A startup operator command (`chd migrate --namespace chd`) performs eager migration by read-highest-rev → write-bumped-rev per key. No in-place mutation of history: old versions remain (D4), so migration is always reversible from namespace git history. A record whose `schema_version` is greater than the running harness supports fails closed on read (`schema_version_unsupported`) rather than being partially interpreted.
**VOLB-049 (retention).** Terminal manifests and closed objective/assignment records are retained ≥ `retention.closed_days` (default 90), then tombstoned by the operator-run compaction (`duckbrain squash` / `forget`), which is also the Parquet-compaction path. Room messages are retained ≥ `retention.room_days` (default 180); standing rules and acceptance criteria are **never auto-retained out** — they are superseded/withdrawn explicitly (state transitions), because they are authority records. Tombstoning (D8) is the only delete mechanism CHD uses, and only for whole-record expiry, never for state transitions.
